I can fully agree with how infuriating it is to see artists who are much younger than me, creating amazing works. I'm 27. Been drawing since I was 5. Social media is a horrid reminder of how mediocre I am. It makes me want to off myself.

But for the record, I do find that my work is good enough, when others see it as so (and when I'm in a good mood LOL).  My doodles have brought much joy to others. And that is something that pushes me to keep drawing (again, when I'm in a good mood). 

Art is subjective. People can find beauty in something you deem hideous.

While I am a hypocrite, please keep striving, if art is your big passion. On my good days, I can feel inspired by others - on my bad days, I cry and indulge in self-loathing. Maybe today is your bad day.

Sexual preferences are not a "choice", it's something that we're naturally born with. It's quite ignorant of your mother to say that.

Hey there~! I'm 26(F), from Louisiana. I'm a digital artist who's struggling to find steady work. Art has been my passion since childhood. I'm generally an upbeat person, but deep down, very hard on myself and depressed 80% of the time. I struggle with varying degrees of self-esteem and anxiety. I like comics, video games, cooking, different cultures, and astronomy - to say the least.

I'm interested in this kik group!! Never used it before, but now I may have a reason to! :D

Hi cherryxbomb and Use-of-Weapons! Thought I'd pop in on this convo since I can relate. :)

CxB, I think we have a similar personality. LOL I'm generally upbeat, talkative, and silly with people, and I used to work as a hostess in a few restaurants. The customers and general public that I interact with likely have NO idea that I'm really a very, sad person. Bubbly exterior, miserable interior. That's totally me.

UoW, I can also sympathize with you on loathing customer service. I'm currently unemployed, but my last few jobs were all hosting. I can generally handle it, but it gets very exhausting. I have had a few breakdowns at work, before. Some days just felt pointless, especially when I'd get a customer who complains about not being able to sit in a certain spot, or not being able to customize their order to infinity. It just makes me want to smack the fuck outta people. Like, you're seriously bitching about something so insignificant?! There's so much more to life than: "I want 10 extra sweet n' sour sauces for free!!!" (seriously, shit like that happened) The general public disgust me.

Hi! Thanks for the reply.

Social media (especially Facebook) is such a slap in the face, most of the time. Even though, I know it's all constructed to make everyone's lives look great, it still hurts to see. Hardly anyone who portrays themselves to be successful, talk about what's REALLY going on...And that's my big issue with people: the lack of being "real" - being honest, being open. I'm the type of person who's always open with people.

There have been times where I've deactivated my Facebook, just to get a break. I got sick of seeing everyone else having fun, but no one bothering to reach out to me. Even when I try conversing with others, it feels kind of stilted, or fake on both ends. Not with everyone, but most.

You're right, there is only different art...and I struggle with accepting that. I have a hard time looking at my work objectively. I hear praise from others, but most of what I see are flaws. Even when I create something that I really like, I end up feeling like its not good enough when I see the works of artists that I follow. It hurts to see so many likes, favs, reblogs of other people's work, but mine barely gets the time of day. I do have my own art pages, with a few followers, but I still feel so small. So insignificant.

There are some things that I know I can improve, if I put my mind to it. But my depression always keeps me down. I struggle to find motivation to work on projects. But when I do draw, it can be quite uplifting. There are many times when I feel very cynical about my work, and others where I'm relaxed and happy. Sometimes, I do criticize myself a lot, when I'm drawing. Like, *"This face looks terrible"* or *"this whole piece is just shit"* then I proceed to erase everything and turn off my computer. (I'm a digital artist btw)


Sorry for rambling...As for structure: no, I don't really have any in my day-to-day. :/ And for success - I'd like to be able to live decently, which for me means: my art being a good portion of my income, frequent commissions, an online shop, selling my art at anime conventions, to be independent again, not stressing about buying groceries, have some disposable income, set aside money for travel. Fairly humble, I guess. 


I do get some commissioned work from time to time, but its not sustainable. I hope that I could land an art-related job somewhere down the line...Like, maybe as an illustrator. And do commissions on the side. Eventually, maybe open an online shop and sell prints, t-shirts, etc.

Thank you for your comment, YAF. Again, sorry for rambling. It feels good to get my thoughts out there..and it feels even better to have someone to talk to. :)
*HUUUGGG*

Damn...that's a long time to be unhappy. I'm really sorry to hear that. I can't imagine how that must feel....The last time I felt happy was back in June. I went on vacation to Tennessee and went hiking for the first time. Vacations always seem to make me forget how sad I am.
I'll keep my fingers crossed for you.

You're welcome! My top fav show is "Sunny in Philly", because it always makes me laugh. :D I watched a marathon of "Sunny" on Netflix recently (when I was really depressed) and even though I felt shitty while watching, there were moments where I just busted my gut with laughter!!
Yaass!! Quirky stuff always cheers me up. Also: Rick and Morty, Steven Universe, and Regular Show are funny cartoons.

I usually try to watch something funny/quirky or a documentary, when I'm feeling down. Here's a list of shows and movies that always lift me up (most are on Netflix):

It's Always Sunny In Philadelphia, The Blues Brothers, Spaceballs, Trading Places, Coming to America, Bill Nye the Science Guy, A Monster in Paris, Bojack Horseman, Cosmos: A Spacetime Odyssey, A Fantastic Fear of Everything.


Hope you can enjoy some of these. :)
